nodes.name: Abort — Malformed Input
nodes.notes: Fails fast with a clear message; triggers the error workflow instead of processing bad data. Watch out: Fails the run on purpose so the Error Workflow fires. This is intentional, not a bug.

nodes.name: Route by Work Type
nodes.notes: Routes each item to one of 4 lanes: standard, priority, batch + fallback. Watch out: Unmatched items go to the fallback output; without one they are silently dropped.

nodes.name: Process 'standard' → Google Sheets
nodes.notes: Upserts a row into 'Payload Tracker', matched on itemId — re-running with the same key updates the row instead of duplicating it. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Fast-Track 'priority' + Alert
nodes.notes: Posts a message to Slack (#ops) — a low-latency way for the team to see automation activity without checking a dashboard. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Slack OAuth2. Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.

nodes.notes: Posts a message to Slack (#ops) — a low-latency way for the team to see automation activity without checking a dashboard. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. nodes.name: Hold Unknown Types (DLQ)
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Payload Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Merge Routed Work
nodes.notes: Rejoins 4 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Tag Pipeline Metadata
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes pipeline, version. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Stamp Processing Time
nodes.notes: Stamps processedAt with the current time for auditing.

nodes.name: Save Execution Metadata
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Cap Batch Volume
nodes.notes: Caps the stream at 100 items to protect downstream quotas.

nodes.name: Sort Payloads Newest First
nodes.notes: Orders items (newest first) so limits and digests pick the most relevant records.

nodes.name: Summarize Run Stats
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes runAt, itemCount, status. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

# Orchestrate a multi-step process: Slack for webhooks

**Pattern:** Workflow Automation · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers webhooks work end to end across Slack, Google Sheets and Gmail.

It moves through 17 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. Daily Schedule
2. Required Fields Present?
3. Abort — Malformed Input
4. Route by Work Type
5. Process 'standard' → Google Sheets
6. Fast-Track 'priority' + Alert
7. Fast-Track 'batch' + Alert
8. Hold Unknown Types (DLQ)
9. Merge Routed Work
10. Tag Pipeline Metadata
11. Stamp Processing Time
12. Save Execution Metadata
13. Cap Batch Volume
14. Sort Payloads Newest First
15. Summarize Run Stats
16. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
17. Send Summary to Gmail

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing webhooks work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Daily Schedule → Required Fields Present? → Abort — Malformed Input → Route by Work Type → Process 'standard' → Google Sheets → Fast-Track 'priority' + Alert → Fast-Track 'batch' + Alert → Hold Unknown Types (DLQ) → Merge Routed Work → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Stamp Processing Time → Save Execution Metadata → Cap Batch Volume → Sort Payloads Newest First → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Gmail → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Slack and Google Sheets aligned by hand for webhooks
- Webhooks work where "Route by Work Type" is still a manual step before Slack
- Webhooks work that only reaches Slack on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Slack and Google Sheets in step for webhooks, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Slack or Google Sheets call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 19 nodes in this webhooks build
- Bad input stops the run for webhooks instead of landing in Slack
- Branches rejoin before Slack, so a webhooks run reports once rather than 19 times
- Every webhooks run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Slack

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2; Google OAuth2 / service account; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Unrecognized work types are parked in a dead-letter lane instead of erroring the whole run or silently dropping the item — new event kinds will show up eventually, and this is where you'd notice one without losing it. One kind is deliberately routed through a sub-workflow to show how heavier per-type logic can be extracted without touching this router at all.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Send a work-type value that matches no switch rule and confirm it lands in the dead-letter branch.
2. Add a new work type and its own handling branch.
3. Replace the direct-write branch with a sub-workflow call, matching the pattern already used for the first kind.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

**Google OAuth2**
Google Cloud Console → enable Gmail API → OAuth consent screen → OAuth client ID (Web).
_Gotcha:_ Add n8n's OAuth redirect URL exactly as shown in the credential, or the consent loop fails.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your webhooks process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Gmail: request the narrowest send/read scope the nodes need — full mailbox access is rarely required.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole webhooks payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
